idiom_name: required keyword arguments + Data.define value objects
implementation_notes: Ruby's required keyword arguments are the local replacement for a staged builder: def initialize(name:, email:) raises ArgumentError when a key is missing, so all required data arrives in one call and ordering becomes irrelevant, while Data.define (Ruby 3.2+) adds immutable value objects with a mandatory constructor and pattern-matching support. The staged chain is hand-written when an API must walk a caller through an expensive or side-effecting sequence: one small class per step, each advancing by constructing the next step, keeps the order visible in the receiver - but the failure for a skipped step is a NoMethodError at run time, not a compile error. Where only presence matters, keyword arguments plus a validated value object are shorter and safer.
code_sketch:
class User
  def initialize(name:, email:, admin: false)   # name/email unskippable
    @name, @email, @admin = name, email, admin
  end
end
User.new(email: "a@b.c")   # ArgumentError: missing keyword: :name

Measure = Data.define(:amount, :unit)   # immutable value object, same idea
Measure.new(100, "km")                  # both members mandatory
pitfalls: A missing required keyword raises only at run time and only on executed paths; a staged chain adds no static safety either, so keep the staging only where the run-time error is acceptable.
Mixing positional and keyword parameters (def initialize(name, email: nil)) silently accepts a nil email - required data must be declared as a keyword without a default.
Struct is mutable (members can be reassigned after construction); Data.define is the immutable variant - and even a Data instance can hold a mutable member, so freeze or dup nested arrays/hashes.
